raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. It's spring here in Quzhou — wheat is already in the ground from last October, maize planting is coming up fast after wheat harvest, and I need to get my stevia sorted out in the next couple weeks.

---

**My reasoning**

I've worked these 6 mu for fifty years now. Just me and the wife at home — kids are in Handan and Shijiazhuang, they send money sometimes but we manage on what the land gives us. At my age I have to be honest about labor. I can still do most things but stevia harvest is hard on the back, so I budget for hired help.

**Land allocation.** I keep 4 mu in stevia because that's where the money is — contracted to the cooperative at a decent price for dried leaf with good stevioside content. The other 2 mu I keep in wheat-maize double cropping. Two mu of wheat gives us more than enough grain for the year with plenty to sell, and the maize sells locally to the pig farmers or goes for feed. I don't want to give up the wheat-maize entirely — grain in the bin is security when the wife and I think about what could go wrong.

**Wheat (2 mu).** I planted Jimai 22 last October on about 15 kg/mu seed rate. Based on the fall stand and what I got last year (480 kg/mu), I'm targeting around 500 kg/mu. My total N is about 20 kg/mu — 12 kg went down as base with DAP before planting, and I'll topdress 8 kg of urea at jointing in mid-March when I do the first spring irrigation. P about 8 kg/mu, K about 5 kg/mu (the soil here holds K reasonably well). Three irrigations: green-up/jointing (March), heading (late April), grain filling if May stays dry. The water meter adds up fast, so I watch the forecast before I turn the pump on. One broadleaf herbicide spray in early spring. If the flowering period turns humid I'll spray tebuconazole once for scab — that decision I make in late April based on what the weather looks like.

**Maize (2 mu).** Right after wheat harvest in early June — we've got maybe 5-7 days. I hire the no-till planter with a neighbor to share the cost; straight into the wheat stubble, keeps the moisture in. Zhengdan 958 seed, about 3 kg/mu. Base fertilizer with the planter — 8 kg N/mu as compound, then 10 kg N/mu as urea topdress at V10-V12 (the large bell stage). Total 18 kg N/mu, targeting 500 kg/mu. I'll irrigate once at tasseling if we don't get rain, maybe a second time at grain fill. Pre-emergence atrazine/acetochlor mix for weeds. I watch for corn borer in July — if I see damage I spray once.

**Stevia (4 mu).** This is the demanding crop. I have 3 mu of 2nd-year plants still producing well, and 1 mu that I'm replanting this year because the stand was thinning. New seedlings go in late April — I get them from the cooperative nursery, about 8000 seedlings per mu, costs me around 800 yuan/mu just for the planting material. The experienced rows need less care but still want fertilizer and water.

On fertilizer — I've learned over the years that stevia doesn't reward heavy nitrogen. Too much N grows big leaves but the stevioside content drops, and the cooperative pays on sugar content. I do about 12 kg N/mu total, split three ways: base before transplant/green-up, after first cut, and after second cut. Phosphorus 6 kg/mu, potassium 10 kg/mu — stevia likes K. Irrigation is where stevia is expensive for me — I need 5-6 waterings through the season, especially right after transplant and after each cut when the plants are regrowing. Two harvests, late June and September. Each harvest I hire 2-3 people for 3-4 days; family labor alone can't handle it at my age. Drying the leaves is the other big job — we use the courtyard and roof, takes about 5 days of good sun.

No pesticides on stevia if I can help it — the buyers test for residue and dock the price. Hand weeding twice in the season.

**Budget and tradeoffs.** Total cash I'll put out this year for inputs runs around 5500 yuan across the 6 mu. The stevia is most of it. If prices hold, net income should be decent — maybe 12-14 thousand from stevia, 2-3 thousand from wheat-maize. The risk is stevia price — if the cooperative drops the contract rate or the sugar content comes in low, that 4 mu earns much less. That's why I keep the 2 mu of grain. If stevia has a bad year, at least we eat.

decision.reasoning_summary: At 68 with just my wife at home, I split 6 mu between 4 mu of stevia (cash crop, contracted to cooperative) and 2 mu of wheat-maize double cropping (food security and insurance). Stevia gets careful moderate N to protect stevioside content, heavy irrigation, and hired labor at harvest — that's where most of my cash goes. Wheat-maize I run efficiently with rates I've refined over decades: 20 kg N/mu wheat split base and jointing topdress, 18 kg N/mu maize split planter-base and bell-stage topdress, no-till maize seeding to catch the 6-day window. The wheat-maize isn't the profit center but keeps grain in the bin if stevia prices disappoint — at my age that security matters more than squeezing another mu into stevia.
